mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 4 Series 435i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement engine for a BMW 435i typically costs between £2,500 and £9,000 depending on condition. Used N55B30A units start from around £2,500, while reconditioned units range from £4,500 to £7,000. Rebuilt engines with warranty sit at £6,000-£9,000. Specialist fitting adds approximately £780-£1,040 in labour.

mainEntity.name: What are the common problems with the BMW 4 Series 435i N55 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The N55 engine in the 435i has several well-documented issues. The most common are charge pipe cracking (plastic pipe becomes brittle), electric water pump failure, oil leaks from the valve cover and oil filter housing gaskets, and VANOS solenoid issues. Carbon buildup on intake valves is also common due to the direct injection system.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 4 Series 435i?

acceptedAnswer.text: A 2013-2016 BMW 435i is typically worth £8,000-£22,000 depending on condition and mileage. If your car is worth over £10,000, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine with warranty is a sound investment - especially if you plan to keep the car for 2+ years. For lower-value examples, a used engine may be more cost-effective.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 4 Series 435i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Supply-only engines are typically dispatched within 1-2 working days. Full supply & fit through a specialist workshop usually takes 2-3 days, depending on workshop availability and the complexity of the specific 435i variant (xDrive models may take slightly longer).

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW 435i and 440i engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 435i uses the N55 3.0-litre inline-six turbo (306hp). The 440i uses the newer B58 3.0-litre inline-six turbo (326hp) which replaced the N55 in 2016 as part of the LCI update. The B58 is generally considered more reliable and more powerful, with fewer known issues.

mainEntity.name: Can I replace my N55 engine with a B58 in my BMW 435i?

acceptedAnswer.text: While both are 3.0-litre inline-six engines, the B58 is not a direct bolt-in replacement for the N55. It requires different engine mounts, wiring looms, ECUs, and cooling systems. It is not a cost-effective or practical swap. Stick with an N55 replacement for your 435i.

historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 435i joined the 4 Series range at launch in 2013 as the range-topping petrol model, offering a smooth and powerful inline-six turbocharged experience. The 435i was powered exclusively by BMW's N55 engine throughout its production run, delivering 306hp and 400Nm of torque.

Production of the 435i ends, replaced by the 440i with the B58 engine as part of the Life Cycle Impulse (LCI) update

commonProblems.h2: BMW 4 Series 435i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 435i is powered exclusively by the N55 3.0-litre turbocharged inline-six - a generally robust engine but one with several well-documented weak points. The most common failures are charge pipe cracking, water pump failure, and oil leaks from various gaskets. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Charge Pipe Cracking - Why the BMW 4 Series 435i N55 Engine Fails
problems.rootCause: The factory charge pipe is made of plastic which becomes brittle and weak after repeated heat cycles, eventually cracking under boost pressure. This causes boost leaks, loss of power, and can trigger the engine management light.

repairOptions.longevity: Budget option; risk of repeat failure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement with aftermarket aluminium charge pipe
repairOptions.longevity: Best long-term fix; eliminates plastic weakness
If charge pipe failure has caused secondary damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2013-2016 BMW 435i is worth approximately £8,000-£22,000 depending on mileage and condition. For cars worth over £10,000, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine usually justifies the premium via warranty and reliability. The charge pipe repair itself is well within the vehicle's value on all but the very lowest-value examples.
problems.recommendation: If you're experiencing loss of power or a check engine light, have the charge pipe inspected immediately. Upgrading to an aluminium charge pipe is a cost-effective preventative measure that eliminates the known weak point.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt N55B30A BMW 4 Series 435i engine prices

problems.h4: Water Pump Failure - BMW 4 Series 435i Cooling System
problems.rootCause: The N55 uses an electric water pump that can fail without warning, causing the engine to overheat and enter limp mode.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement electric water pump, coolant flush, system bleed
repairOptions.longevity: Preventative replacement at 60k miles or at first sign of overheating
If overheating has caused warped head or other damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a 435i valued at £8,000-£22,000, the water pump repair is well within the vehicle's value. Preventative replacement is strongly recommended.
problems.recommendation: Replace the water pump proactively at around 60,000 miles - it's far cheaper than dealing with the consequences of an overheat. Always use genuine or OEM-spec parts.
